title: Saltimbocca alla Romana
subtitle: Roman chicken with prosciutto and sage
excerpt: Saltimbocca means 'jump in the mouth' -- a fair description of how fast this dish disappears. Thin chicken escalopes are wrapped in prosciutto and sage, then pan-fried in butter and finished with a sharp white wine sauce. It takes under 20 minutes.
sourceNotes: Saltimbocca alla Romana is a Roman classic, traditionally made with veal. Chicken breast or turkey escalopes are excellent substitutes and much more common outside Italy.

content.text: Bash the chicken flat before cooking -- an even thickness means it cooks through without drying out. The prosciutto should be pressed firmly against the chicken. Use a cocktail stick if needed.

items.prepNote: sliced in half horizontally to make 8 thin escalopes

content.text: Place each chicken escalope between two sheets of cling film. Bash with a rolling pin to about 5mm thick. Season lightly.
Lay a sage leaf on each escalope. Press a slice of prosciutto over the top. Press firmly so the prosciutto adheres.
Heat the butter and oil in a wide frying pan over medium-high heat. Place the escalopes prosciutto-side down. Cook for 3 minutes until the prosciutto is golden and crisp.
Flip the escalopes. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the chicken is cooked through. Remove and keep warm.
Pour the wine into the hot pan. Scrape up any browned bits. Let it bubble for 2 minutes until reduced by half. Add a squeeze of lemon and swirl in the remaining butter.
Pour the pan sauce over the chicken. Serve immediately with green vegetables or roasted potatoes.

items.fix: Press the prosciutto firmly onto the chicken. If it keeps sliding, secure with a cocktail stick through the side.

items.cause: Overcooked -- thin escalopes cook very fast
items.fix: Cook for 2 to 3 minutes per side maximum. The prosciutto side should be golden; the plain side just turns white through.

content.text: Saltimbocca is Roman. The veal original is rarely seen outside Italy. Chicken works just as well and is far more accessible. It is a restaurant dish that is very easy to replicate at home.
